tutorial.title: HTTP Request Responses
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn about server responses to a GET request, including status codes.

lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent:
So far we've looked at the GET request that a client sends to the server to retrieve data.

Let's move on to the possible responses a server can send.

lessons.title: GET Request
lessons.interactiveContent:
In sending this GET request, the client wants to retrieve information about the courses Mimo offers stored in the server's database.

We can communicate with our own servers or with others. However, some servers restrict the usage.

Make sure to pick GET.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The client wants to retrieve information about the courses Mimo offers from the server’s database. Choose the request method.

We can communicate with our own servers or with others. However, some servers restrict the usage.

Make sure to pick GET.

lessons.title: Receiving request
lessons.interactiveContent:
When the server receives this request, it checks whether the route /courses exists and whether it can return the requested data.

Make sure to pick /courses.
lessons.hardModeContent:
When the server receives this request, it checks whether the route /courses exists and whether it can return the requested data.

Make sure to pick fetch, followed by /courses, and finally .then.

lessons.title: Server response
lessons.interactiveContent:
Typically, the server responds with a status and the requested data. If the server can deliver data for the request, the status is 200 OK.

Make sure to pick 200, followed by OK.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Typically, the server responds with a status and the requested data. If the server can deliver data for the request, the status is 200 OK.

Make sure to pick 200, followed by OK.

lessons.title: Response parts
lessons.interactiveContent:
Actually, the API sends back more data. There are three parts: the status line, the headers, and the body.

The headers contain information about the response, and the body holds the actual data, like the user information you requested.

Make sure to pick STATUS:, followed by HEADERS:, and finally BODY:.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Actually, the API sends back more data. There are three parts: the status line, the headers, and the body.

The headers contain information about the response, and the body holds the actual data, like the user information you requested.

Make sure to pick STATUS:, followed by HEADERS:, and finally BODY:.

lessons.title: Receiving request - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Log the response to see what the server returns.

Make sure to pick response.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Log the response to see what the server returns.

Make sure to pick .then, followed by response.

lessons.title: Question: Receiving request
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is one of the things a server does when receiving a GET request?

It checks if the route exists and if it can return the requested dataIt returns a random resource for testing purposes

It checks if the route exists and if it can return the requested data.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A client sends a GET request for /courses. What does the server check before returning the course data?

Whether the route exists and the requested data can be returnedWhether the client already has a copy of every courseWhether the GET request contains data to save at that route

Whether the route exists and the requested data can be returned.

lessons.title: Question: Response parts
lessons.interactiveContent:
What are the parts of an HTTP response like the one below?

Status line, headers, and the response bodyRequest method and protocol

Status line, headers, and the response body.
lessons.hardModeContent:
How should you classify Status: 200 OK, Content-Type: application/json, and the courses JSON in this response?

Status line, header, and response bodyRequest method, route, and request bodyHeader, response body, and status line

Status line, header, and response body.

lessons.title: Example: GET Request
lessons.interactiveContent:
Log the response object that you get back when calling the GET endpoint /courses.

Make sure to pick response followed by console.log( and then response, );.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Log the response object that you get back when calling the GET endpoint /courses.

Make sure to pick response, followed by console.log(, response, and finally );.

lessons.title: Example: Response parts
lessons.interactiveContent:
This is an HTTP response to a successful GET request. Code the status line.

Make sure to pick 200, followed by OK.
lessons.hardModeContent:
This is an HTTP response to a successful GET request. Code the status line.

Make sure to pick 200, followed by OK.

lessons.title: Status code
lessons.interactiveContent:
A response's status code tells us whether our request was successful or not. 200 OK means that our GET request succeeded.

Make sure to pick 200, followed by OK.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A response's status code tells us whether our request was successful or not. 200 OK means that our GET request succeeded.

Make sure to pick 200, followed by OK.

lessons.title: 400 Bad Request
lessons.interactiveContent:
Some status codes tell us that something went wrong in the client-server communication, like 400.

400 Bad Request means that the server could not understand our request due to an invalid syntax, like a typo in our URL.

Make sure to pick 400, followed by Bad Request.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Some status codes tell us that something went wrong in the client-server communication, like 400.

400 Bad Request means that the server could not understand our request due to an invalid syntax, like a typo in our URL.

Make sure to pick 400, followed by Bad Request.

lessons.title: 401 Unauthorized
lessons.interactiveContent:
401 Unauthorized, comes up when the client requests a resource that's not available without logging in, like a user's private messages.

Make sure to pick 401, followed by Unauthorized.
lessons.hardModeContent:
401 Unauthorized, comes up when the client requests a resource that's not available without logging in, like a user's private messages.

Make sure to pick 401, followed by Unauthorized.

lessons.title: 404 Not Found
lessons.interactiveContent:
404 Not Found is another frequent error status code, meaning that the server couldn't find the data that the client requested.

Make sure to pick 404, followed by Not Found.
lessons.hardModeContent:
404 Not Found is another frequent error status code, meaning that the server couldn't find the data that the client requested.

Make sure to pick 404, followed by Not Found.

lessons.title: Client errors
lessons.interactiveContent:
Error status codes in the range of 400-499 are called client errors, indicating that something went wrong on the client side.

Make sure to pick Bad Request, followed by Unauthorized, and finally Not Found.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Error status codes in the range of 400-499 are called client errors, indicating that something went wrong on the client side.

Make sure to pick Bad Request, followed by Unauthorized, and finally Not Found.

lessons.title: Server errors
lessons.interactiveContent:
Codes in the range of 500-599 are server errors, like 500 Internal Server Error.

Make sure to pick 500, followed by Internal Server Error.

lessons.title: Question: Status code
lessons.interactiveContent:
What do status codes tell us?

Whether our request was successful or not, and whyWhether the client sent a request

Whether our request was successful or not, and why.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A GET request receives 404 Not Found. What information does this status communicate?

The request was unsuccessful because the resource was not foundThe client did not send a request to the serverThe response body must contain an empty JSON object

The request was unsuccessful because the resource was not found.

lessons.title: Question: 400 Bad Request
lessons.interactiveContent:
When might we get a 400 Bad Request status after sending a GET request?

When our request is syntactically incorrect, for example, because of a typoWhen the server doesn't have the resource we requested

When our request is syntactically incorrect, for example, because of a typo.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which GET request problem could produce 400 Bad Request?

A typo makes the request syntax invalidThe requested course does not exist on the serverThe server crashes while processing a valid request

A typo makes the request syntax invalid.

lessons.title: Question: 401 Unauthorized
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which of these scenarios might end up with a 401 Unauthorized response code?

Requesting a user's home address before logging inRequesting a user's home address after logging in

Requesting a user's home address before logging in.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which request is most likely to receive 401 Unauthorized?

Requesting a user's home address without logging inRequesting a user's home address with valid login credentialsRequesting a public profile that does not exist

Requesting a user's home address without logging in.

lessons.title: Question: 404 Not Found
lessons.interactiveContent:
When might we get a 404 Not Found status after sending a GET request?

When the server doesn't have the resource we're requestingWhen we're not allowed to access the resource we're requesting

When the server doesn't have the resource we're requesting.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which GET request should produce 404 Not Found?

Requesting /courses/999 when course 999 does not existRequesting a private course without logging inSending a course ID with invalid request syntax

Requesting /courses/999 when course 999 does not exist.

lessons.title: Question: Client errors
lessons.interactiveContent:
What are error codes in the range of 400-499 generally called?

Client errorsServer errors

Client errors.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Status codes from 400 to 499 are called client errors.

A response has status code 418. Which error category does its range place it in?

Client errorServer errorSuccessful response

Make sure to pick Client error.

lessons.title: Question: Server errors
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's an example of a server error code?

500400

Make sure to pick 500.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The server crashes while handling a valid GET request. Which status code fits this server error?

500400404

Make sure to pick 500.

lessons.title: Example: Status code
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code a successful status code for this response to a GET request.

Make sure to pick 200.

lessons.title: Example: 400 Bad Request
lessons.interactiveContent:
There was something wrong with the syntax of our request, so the server sent back a 400 Bad Request.

Make sure to pick 400, followed by Bad Request.

lessons.title: Example: 401 Unauthorized
lessons.interactiveContent:
Pick a status code we'd get if we tried to access a user's wishlist without being logged in.

Make sure to pick 401 Unauthorized.
lessons.hardModeContent:
401 Unauthorized means the requested resource requires logging in.

Your wishlist request succeeded while you were logged in. You sign out and request it again. Complete both statuses.

Make sure to pick 200 OK, followed by 401 Unauthorized.

lessons.title: Example: 404 Not Found
lessons.interactiveContent:
Pick a status code we'd get if we tried to access an item that the server doesn't have in its database.

Make sure to pick 404 Not Found.
lessons.hardModeContent:
404 Not Found means the server could not find the requested item.

The item request succeeded. The item is then deleted. Complete the statuses before and after deletion.

Make sure to pick 200 OK, followed by 404 Not Found.

lessons.title: Successful request
lessons.interactiveContent: Let's look at the response body. If the request is successful, the client will receive 200 OK and a response body containing the data.

lessons.title: JSON
lessons.interactiveContent:
One common format for an HTTP response body is JSON, which stands for JavaScript Object Notation.

Under the hood, it's a JavaScript object.

Make sure to pick {, followed by "courses":, and finally }.
lessons.hardModeContent:
One common format for an HTTP response body is JSON, which stands for JavaScript Object Notation.

Under the hood, it's a JavaScript object.

Make sure to pick {, followed by "courses":, and finally }.

lessons.title: JSON 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
The JSON syntax is similar to that of a JavaScript object. Here, you can see the same object, first in JSON, and then in Javascript.

Can you spot the difference?

Make sure to pick " followed by " and then ", ".
lessons.hardModeContent:
The JSON syntax is similar to that of a JavaScript object. Here, you can see the same object, first in JSON, and then in Javascript.

Can you spot the difference?

Make sure to pick ", followed by ", ", and finally ".

lessons.title: JSON properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we receive 200 OK, we can expect the response object to include the data we asked for.

In the case of calling https://mimo.org/courses, it's an array of courses.

Make sure to pick "courses", followed by [, and finally ].
lessons.hardModeContent:
If we receive 200 OK, we can expect the response object to include the data we asked for.

Complete the JSON response body from https://mimo.org/courses, containing an array named courses.

Make sure to pick "courses", followed by [, and finally ].

lessons.title: Unsuccessful request
lessons.interactiveContent:
In case of an error, a GET request still gets a response with an error code, but not the requested data.

Make sure to pick 400, followed by Bad Request.
lessons.hardModeContent:
In case of an error, a GET request still gets a response with an error code, but not the requested data.

The first line is a status summary, not an HTTP response header. Complete the 400 Bad Request summary and the JSON header.

Make sure to pick 400 Bad Request, followed by Content-Type.

lessons.title: Question: Successful request
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is in the response body of a server's response to a GET request?

The data that the client requestedHeaders offering information about the response format

The data that the client requested.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A GET request returns a list of courses and a Content-Type header. Which part is the response body?

The list of courses that the client requested.The Content-Type header that describes the response format.The status code that reports whether the request succeeded.

The list of courses that the client requested.

lessons.title: Question: JSON
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's a common format used for an HTTP response body?

JSONJavaScript

Make sure to pick JSON.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A server sends {"courses": []} as the response body. Which common body format does this use?

JSONJavaScriptAn HTTP status line

Make sure to pick JSON.

lessons.title: Question: Unsuccessful request
lessons.interactiveContent:
Do we still get the requested data if we get an error status code?

No, we can't get the data because the request failedYes, we get the data anyway

No, we can't get the data because the request failed.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A GET request returns 400 Bad Request and no course list. What can the client conclude about the requested data?

It cannot get the requested data because the request failed.The requested data is available because the server sent a response.The requested data is stored in the status code.

It cannot get the requested data because the request failed.

lessons.title: Example: JSON
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code curly braces around this JSON object to complete the object structure.

Make sure to pick {, followed by }.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete the outer JSON object and the list that holds the courses.

Make sure to pick {, followed by [, ], and finally }.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's the difference between JSON and JavaScript objects?

JSON has quotes " " around property names like "username"JSON separates properties and values with a :

JSON has quotes " " around property names like "username".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Compare {"username": "Mia"} with a JavaScript object using the same property. Which detail makes the first one JSON?

Its property name is enclosed in double quotes.It separates the property and value with a colon.It stores a text value in double quotes.

Its property name is enclosed in double quotes.
